einzeiler: Unearthing James Wilson, the forgotten founding father who championed popular sovereignty.
kurzfassung: James Wilson was a Scottish immigrant and brilliant legal mind who played a central role in drafting the American Constitution and the Declaration of Independence. Despite pioneering the concept of popular sovereignty, his abrasive personality, massive land speculation debts, and dramatic downfall caused him to be largely erased from mainstream history. Author Jesse Wegman discusses Wilson's immense yet overlooked contributions to American democracy on American History Hit.
stichpunkte: James Wilson was a Scottish immigrant who brought advanced Enlightenment ideas to America.
He argued that all lawful government is founded on the consent of the governed, predating key phrases in the Declaration of Independence.
Wilson proposed the direct election of the president during the Constitutional Convention before ultimately drafting the Electoral College compromise.
He strongly opposed the Senate's equal state representation, warning it would lead to perpetual error and disease.
Wilson introduced the phrase 'We the People' and authored the supremacy and necessary and proper clauses in the Constitution.
Despite his immense legal contributions, aggressive land speculation left him bankrupt and imprisoned for debt.
He became the only U.S. Supreme Court justice to see the inside of a prison cell before dying in obscurity in 1798.

clips.text: Due to a local educational system focused on ensuring all children learned basic literacy regardless of social standing, Scotland boasted the highest reading rates in Europe.

clips.hook: Behind the famous portrait of the founders
clips.text: Popular imagination envisions the founding documents emerging from harmonious agreement, whereas reality involved months of intense, grueling arguments and scattered paperwork.
The iconic opening phrase of the Constitution was specifically placed at the forefront of the document to anchor it firmly in the democratic spirit of popular sovereignty.

clips.hook: A democratic state constitution opposed by a democrat
clips.text: Pennsylvania enacted the most democratic state constitution in the nation's history in 1776, yet Wilson actively opposed it despite his broader political beliefs.

clips.hook: A Supreme Court justice behind bars
clips.text: Crushed by enormous debts from failed land speculations, a sitting member of the United States Supreme Court ended up locked inside a debtors' prison.

beschreibung:
Signatory of both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution, James Wilson was a sitting Supreme Court justice when he died. So why is he missing from popular history?

From inspiring the phrase 'we the people' to starting the ball rolling on the Electoral College, Jesse Wegman joins Don to discuss Wilson's influence on the United States.

Jesse is Senior Fellow at the Brennan Center for Justice and author of 'The Lost Founder: James Wilson and the Forgotten Fight for a People's Constitution'.
